proposal: The Mandate recommends reinstating the three 2018 Trump labor orders (EOs 13836, 13837, 13839) to renegotiate union contracts around management rights, curb official time for union activity, and limit grievances over removals and appraisals. status_summary: The administration did not reinstate the 2018 orders by name; OPM said on 2025-02-07 that revoking Biden's EO 14003 did not by itself reinstate them. Instead EO 14251 (2025-03-27) and EO 14343 (2025-08-28) excluded dozens of agencies and subdivisions from the federal labor-relations statute on national security grounds, and an OPM memo of 2026-02-12 (revised 2026-02-17) told covered agencies to terminate their collective bargaining agreements, except for units protected by court orders, and to report monthly. The Ninth Circuit vacated the preliminary injunction in AFGE v. Trump on 2026-02-26, but injunctions remain for some units (for example DoD Education Activity and a VA master agreement), and the D.C. Circuit had not ruled as of late September 2026 on appeals argued 2025-12-15. On 2026-09-22 the FLRA dismissed a Defense Department case for lack of jurisdiction under the orders. FSIP members were appointed in July 2026 and an FLRA General Counsel was confirmed on 2026-08-07. On about 2026-10-02 a First Circuit panel stayed a district order that had treated the VA agreements with AFGE as extended, which may let them expire; in Connecticut a federal judge ordered the Bureau of Prisons in late September 2026 to restore its AFGE agreements, and the Bureau issued a new termination notice on 2026-10-07.

timeline.event: OPM Acting Director issued a memo stating that Executive Order 14171 had revoked EO 14003 (which had rescinded EOs 13836, 13837 and 13839) and that the revocation did not itself reinstate the rescinded orders, while directing agencies to return to first-term discipline and performance policies.

EO 14251 (90 FR 14553, published 2025-04-03) adds national security exclusions to the federal labor-management relations program for about 40 agencies and subdivisions; Sec. 6 requires reassignment of employees doing non-agency union business (official time) when a contract is terminated.

EO 14343 (90 FR 42683, published 2025-09-03) excludes additional agencies and subdivisions from the labor-relations program, including the Bureau of Reclamation hydropower units, parts of Commerce (International Trade Administration, Patent and Trademark Office units, National Weather Service), NASA and the U.S. Agency for Global Media.

The House passed H.R. 2550, the Protect America's Workforce Act, 231 to 195 (Roll no. 332) after considering it under H. Res. 432; the bill would nullify EO 14251. It was received in the Senate on 2025-12-15 with no further action listed.

OPM Director's memo (issued 2026-02-12, revised 2026-02-17) tells agencies covered by EOs 14251 and 14343 to notify unions that applicable collective bargaining agreements are terminated, to report the status of every unit on the first of each month until done, and not to apply the guidance to units under a current court order; the memo does not address official time.

Ninth Circuit panel (Judges Owens, Bade and Bress) in AFGE v. Trump (No. 25-4014) vacates the preliminary injunction against EO 14251, holding that the government showed the order would have issued absent any retaliatory motive given its national security rationale; it expressed no view on an ultra vires claim, and merits proceedings remain.

A First Circuit panel stays a district court order that the VA contract with AFGE had automatically extended past August 2026; it expressed no view on the pending appeal of the earlier injunction (about 2026-10-02, reported 2026-10-05).

title: Limit federal employee unions: bargaining scope, official time, FLRA staffing
uncertainties: Official time: apart from EO 14251 Sec. 6, OPM's FY2025 official-time reporting call (due 2026-02-23) and the July 2026 OPM/MSPB proposed rule (which would bar official time to represent colleagues in covered proceedings), no standalone official-time order matching EO 13837 was found; this was not searched exhaustively. On 2026-09-22 the FLRA voted 2-1 to dismiss a DoD case for lack of jurisdiction because DoD is covered by the orders (per Government Executive). The current status of the Rhode Island VA case after May 2026, and the number of contracts actually terminated could not be confirmed. The share of the workforce affected is reported inconsistently across articles. Update 2026-10-15: the D. Conn. Bureau of Prisons injunction and the 2026-10-07 re-termination are confirmed by two Government Executive reports (2026-10-06 and 2026-10-08); the exact injunction date (2026-09-29) and a contempt hearing set for 2026-10-13 rest on a tracker (FedTools) only, and no outcome of the contempt motion was found. The First Circuit VA order is dated only as a Friday in a report of 2026-10-05. No D.C. Circuit decision in NTEU or AFSA was found. S. 2837 sits in committee. Primary lift: the text of EO 14251's Federal Register record, the EO 14343 Federal Register page, the OPM memos of 2025-02-07 and 2026-02-12, the Ninth Circuit opinion of 2026-02-26 and both FLRA press releases were read and match the record; the OPM 2026 memo does not address official time, and EO 14343 contains no official-time provision.
